findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0355: References to Unauthorized Database Access through Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
owncloudApp/src/qa/AndroidManifest.xml:20: provider com.owncloud.android.test.TestPreferencesProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.explanation:

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
BiometricPrompt gets a CryptoObject, but the cipher is never used for a cryptographic operation. Success is decided by comparing object references in onAuthenticationSucceeded, so the unlock is event-bound in practice.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/security/biometric/BiometricActivity.kt:91: Unlock decided by object comparison in the callback; no encrypt/decrypt with the authenticated cipher.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0272: Identify Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the Android Project
MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
FileContentProvider concatenates uri.pathSegments into SQL with appendWhere without parameterization. The provider is android:exported="false", so only the app itself can reach it.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/providers/FileContentProvider.kt:332: URI path segment concatenated into WHERE clause.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
The privacy-policy WebView has JavaScript enabled and gets a WebViewClient that overrides neither shouldOverrideUrlLoading nor shouldInterceptRequest. Any link in the loaded page then opens inside the in-app WebView, with no restriction to trusted hosts.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/settings/privacypolicy/PrivacyPolicyActivity.kt:87: WebViewClient without URL-loading restriction.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0217: Insecure TLS Protocols Explicitly Allowed in Code
findings.explanation:
HttpClient explicitly falls back to SSLContext TLSv1.1/TLSv1.0, and TLSSocketFactory enables TLSv1.1 on sockets. The fallback only runs when TLS 1.2 is unavailable, and TLSSocketFactory has no callers.
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/common/http/HttpClient.java:109: Explicit fallback to TLS 1.1 (then 1.0 on line 112).
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/common/http/TLSSocketFactory.java:78: TLSv1.1 explicitly enabled on sockets.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
When a server is not reachable over TLS, the server base URL is built with http:// and used for all WebDAV/API traffic. The base-config permits cleartext, so these requests go out unencrypted.
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/common/network/WebdavUtils.java:111: Non-SSL servers get an http:// base URL used for communication.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
owncloudApp/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
AdvancedX509TrustManager skips all validation (chain, trust and expiry) for any certificate in the 'known servers' store, i.e. self-signed or untrusted certs the user accepted earlier. This deliberately loosens trust.
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/common/network/AdvancedX509TrustManager.java:99: Certificates in the known-servers store bypass standard trust and validity checks.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
KnownServersHostnameVerifier returns true for any hostname when the peer certificate is in the known-servers store, so a certificate accepted for one server is trusted for every host.
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/common/network/KnownServersHostnameVerifier.java:55: Hostname mismatch accepted if the certificate is in the known store, regardless of host.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0285: Outdated Android Version Allowing Trust in User-Provided CAs
findings.explanation:
The network security config trusts user-installed CAs outside debug-overrides, so anyone who can install a certificate on the device can read the app's TLS traffic.
owncloudApp/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:5: base-config trusts user-installed CAs

findings.explanation:

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0254: Dangerous App Permissions
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is requested without maxSdkVersion, though on scoped-storage versions the app uses app-private storage and MediaStore. POST_NOTIFICATIONS is justified by transfer notifications. Ward's analyzer said: Dangerous (runtime) permissions requested. Check that each is needed for a feature, and that a weaker one (coarse instead of fine location, foreground instead of background) would not do.
owncloudApp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:25: Dangerous storage permission with no maxSdkVersion limit.
owncloudApp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:25: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
owncloudApp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:30: android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared and LogsListActivity copies app log files unencrypted into the shared Downloads collection via MediaStore; those logs contain OAuth access/refresh tokens (see MASTG-TEST-0231).
owncloudApp/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:25: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE declared with no maxSdkVersion.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/logging/LogsListActivity.kt:161: Log file is written unencrypted to shared Downloads via MediaStore.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/authentication/AccountAuthenticator.java:443: The logs being exported contain new access and refresh tokens.

findings.title: MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package
findings.explanation:
An OAuth2 client secret is hardcoded in a string resource shipped in the APK and used for token refresh when no dynamically registered secret is stored.
owncloudApp/src/main/res/values/setup.xml:95: Hardcoded OAuth2 client secret in resources.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
Timber logs OAuth refresh tokens, new access tokens, authorization codes and full token responses; OCFileLoggingTree writes these to log files that the user can export.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/authentication/AccountAuthenticator.java:331: Refresh token logged in clear.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/authentication/AccountAuthenticator.java:443: New access and refresh tokens logged in clear.
owncloudApp/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/presentation/authentication/LoginActivity.kt:628: OAuth authorization code logged.
owncloudComLibrary/src/main/java/com/owncloud/android/lib/resources/oauth/TokenRequestRemoteOperation.kt:72: Full token response logged.
